If you're a Dallas Cowboys fan of a certain age, you can say without question: The Randy White years were the team's best, hands down.

There's no debate. But if one begins, you can direct all detractors to your Cowboys memorabilia collection - complete with this signed and authenticated jersey.

After playing for the University of Maryland Terrapins, White was drafted by the Cowboys in 1975 as a first-round pick. He served as a backup for his first couple of years on the field, before recognition started to build in 1976. That year, he earned a spot on an All-Pro team, an appearance at a Pro Bowl, and a co-MVP award following Super Bowl XII. By 1978, the NFC named him Defensive Player of the Year.

White continued playing into the 1988 season. In total, he played 14 seasons and 209 games - the second-longest streak at that time for anyone who signed with Dallas.

column2: Michael Vick Signed Atlanta White Football Jersey (Beckett)
column3:
Whether you track a team's changing lineup or a player's career trajectory, nothing is quite like holding onto a milestone from their history.

Atlanta Falcons and Michael Vick fans eager to grow their collections will find that connection in this autographed jersey. Vick spent 13 seasons in the National Football League (NFL), beginning his professional career after the Falcons drafted him in 2001.

Years before that, Vick developed a rising reputation as a high school player and then for Virginia Tech, where he received the Archie Griffin Award as a freshman.

Vick continued his stride for the Falcons, spending six years with the team and taking them to two playoffs, a division title and an NFC Championship Game. He also became the NFL's first quarterback to rush 1,000 yards in a single season - a record held until his retirement in 2017.

While Vick had stints on other teams - most notably, the Philadelphia Eagles - his post-professional career saw him loop back to Atlanta. There, he coached the Atlanta Legends, an Alliance of American Football team, until late 2024, when Norfolk State University appointed him their head football coach.

This autographed white Michael Vick jersey captures his early years in the NFL and includes both his player number and signature on the back.
